clue.text: Greek character caught, despite being smart

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone is caught out but remains stylish all the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart and stylish are synonyms describing elegant dress.

clue.text: The extent of the region

explanation.definitionFit: The measured size of a surface is its area, and a district or zone is also called an area.

clue.text: The net used in the home's hard-wearing

indicators.note: the letters needed are used within the run of clue words that follows

explanation.surface: Netting fitted around the house is tough and durable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' points inside 'home's hard': hoME'S Hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesh is an open fabric of threads, the same thing as netting.

clue.text: A serving man once raced to serve

indicators.note: the words raced to are made to serve a new purpose, rearranged into a fresh word

explanation.surface: A waiter of old hurried off to wait at table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serve' asks the letters of RACED TO to be put to new use as an anagram. A REDCOAT was a British soldier of earlier centuries, named for his scarlet tunic.
explanation.definitionFit: A British soldier in former times wore a scarlet coat and so was called by that nickname; a soldier is a man serving.

clue.text: He makes deals with many operating farm machinery

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
a machine that is operating is on
a tractor is the standard farm vehicle

explanation.surface: A dealer who drives tractors around the farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A builder or supplier who agrees a contract for work is a person who makes deals.

clue.text: Don't fill up so often for nothing

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means recharge less often, as with a battery; as one word it means free of cost.

clue.text: Stand-off brought about by worn-out fellow

parts.note: worn-out jokes or ideas are stale
a mate is a companion or fellow

explanation.surface: A deadlock caused by a tired-out companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock in which neither side can advance is a stand-off, from the chess position.

clue.text: Cut the yield

explanation.definitionFit: To trim short is to crop, and the harvest a field produces is its crop.

clue.text: Held to be acted on in error

indicators.note: something done in error goes wrong, so these letters come out scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone detained so that a mistake could be put right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in error' signals an anagram of ACTED ON IN; the second 'in' is fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held within limits is restrained or enclosed.

clue.text: Dance, taking drink after drink after drink

parts.note: cha is an informal word for tea
cha again, another cup of tea
cha a third time, tea once more

explanation.surface: A dancer downs one drink after another.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is British slang for tea; three of them in a row give the Latin dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha-cha is a Latin American ballroom dance.

clue.text: Article follows about tin

indicators.note: the article comes after the letter for about

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A news article comes out on the subject of tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin is a metal container for food, the same as a can.

clue.text: A record some youngsters cannot endure

indicators.note: only some of the letters in these words are taken, a run tucked inside them

explanation.surface: There is a feat that some young people cannot bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' points to a run inside 'cannot endure': canNOT Endure.
explanation.definitionFit: A written memorandum or jotting is a brief record.

clue.text: A great many left to retire

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the word to is read backwards

explanation.surface: Lots of people have left work to retire.
explanation.definitionFit: A large quantity is informally a lot, as in a lot of people.

clue.text: Bring back army personnel-favoured by the government

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
someone favoured is in, in fashion or in favour
the state is the nation's government

explanation.surface: Troops being restored to duty with official backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore someone to a former post is to bring them back.

clue.text: Respecting a black holding on, as is quite right

parts.note: re means concerning or respecting, as in business letters

indicators.note: the word for black holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: sable is black in heraldry
taken as written

explanation.surface: Showing a black person due respect while holding on is quite correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts ON inside SABLE, the heraldic word for black, giving SONABLE after RE and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fair and sensible is justified, quite right in the circumstances.

clue.text: Dreamers who are thought heels

parts.note: an idea is a thought
a ship that heels leans over, or lists

explanation.surface: Visionaries are held to be cads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heels' looks like the noun for cads but is the verb: a ship heels, or lists, when it tilts.
explanation.definitionFit: Visionaries who pursue perfect ideals are often called dreamers.

clue.text: Calm a good man with some affliction

parts.note: ST, short for saint, is a crossword stand-in for a good man
an illness is an affliction

explanation.surface: A good man stays serene despite suffering from disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm as a noun means quietness or tranquillity, the absence of motion.

clue.text: The man coming to a stop

parts.note: a dam stops the flow of water

explanation.surface: A fellow coming to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first man is named Adam, so he is the man.

clue.text: Girl models are evil!

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so these letters are shaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone declares that fashion models are wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'models' looks like a noun but is the verb shaping ARE EVIL into a new word.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, given here as an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: Voice complaint over traps for sea-birds

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for complaining is read backwards

parts.note: to nag is to voice a complaint repeatedly
nets are traps for fish or birds

explanation.surface: Someone protests about snares set for seabirds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns NAG round to give GAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Large white diving seabirds of the North Atlantic are called gannets.

clue.text: Looks for a soft fruit

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for soft
pears are a common orchard fruit

explanation.surface: Someone is searching for a piece of soft fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looks for' wants to mean searching, but 'Looks' is the definition and 'for' a link; 'soft' is P, the musical abbreviation for piano.
explanation.definitionFit: To look a certain way is to seem, giving the outward impression.

clue.text: Game put together

explanation.definitionFit: Pool is a cue game played on a table, and to pool resources is to combine them.

clue.text: An individual seeing what others have to say

definitions.text: An individual seeing what others have to say

parts.words: An individual seeing what others have to say
parts.note: reads like a good listener, but literally describes a deaf person who sees speech on the mouths of others

explanation.surface: A person who sees the point of what others say.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who follows speech by watching mouth movements understands it by sight.

clue.text: Atmosphere causing strain?

explanation.definitionFit: The gases around us form the atmosphere, and a tune or melody is a strain.

clue.text: Small hotel in the Norwegian capital

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the capital, or head letter, of the word Norwegian is taken

explanation.surface: A guest house in Oslo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' wants Oslo, but it means the first letter of 'Norwegian'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub offering rooms is a small hotel or tavern.

clue.text: Qualify for a free ticket

explanation.definitionFit: To succeed in an exam is to qualify, and a pass is a permit for free entry or travel.

clue.text: Watches exercise when there's a problem in sight

parts.note: to eye is to watch
to train is to exercise

explanation.surface: Watching a workout can become a problem for your vision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watches' looks like timepieces but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiredness of the eyes from overuse is a common problem affecting vision.

clue.text: Change 11, though sound

indicators.note: change tells the solver to alter the order of the letters from that answer

parts.note: the clue number refers to the answer to 11 across

explanation.surface: Altering the eleventh clue still sounds right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' signals an anagram of the answer to 11 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical pitch or quality of voice is a sound.

clue.text: To every one the youth-leader is a friend

parts.note: all means every one

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter of the word youth

explanation.surface: A youth leader befriends everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter or associate on your side is a friend.

clue.text: Darling dog responsible for guarding children

definitions.text: Darling dog responsible for guarding children

parts.words: Darling dog responsible for guarding children
parts.note: reads as a sweet guard dog, but Darling is the family name in Peter Pan whose nursemaid is a dog

explanation.surface: A lovely dog looks after the youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: In J. M. Barrie's Peter Pan, the Darling children are minded by a Newfoundland dog; a granny is also informally called this.
explanation.definitionFit: The Darling family's canine nursemaid in Barrie's story bears this name.

clue.text: The French going in for alcoholic liquor

indicators.note: the French word goes inside the word for for

parts.note: as can mean for, as in taking something as or for a joke
le is French for the

explanation.surface: The French are taking up strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going in' puts LE inside AS; 'for' is not a link here but gives AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Beers brewed with top-fermenting yeast are alcoholic drinks.

clue.text: Breath-taking crime!

parts.note: breathtaking usually means amazing, but here it literally describes choking someone

explanation.surface: An astonishing offence!
explanation.definitionFit: Throttling someone stops their breathing, a violent offence.
